parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *enthalpy change of atomisation*.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The overall reaction for the atomisation of liquid bromine molecules, $\text{Br}_2\text{(l)}$, is shown.

$$\text{Br}_2\text{(l)} \rightarrow 2\text{Br}\text{(g)}$$

This happens via a two-step process.

- Construct a **labelled** energy cycle to represent this atomisation process, including state symbols.
- Use your cycle and relevant data from the *Data Booklet* to calculate the enthalpy change of vaporisation of $\text{Br}_2\text{(l)}$, $\Delta H^{\ominus}_{\text{vap}}$.
The enthalpy change of atomisation of bromine, $\Delta H_{\text{at}} = +112\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Suggest how the $\Delta H^{\ominus}_{\text{vap}}$ of iodine, $\text{I}_2\text{(l)}$, would compare to that of bromine, $\text{Br}_2\text{(l)}$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *enthalpy change of hydration*.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why the enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Br}^-\text{(g)}$ is **more** exothermic than that of $\text{I}^-\text{(g)}$.
